nodes.label: No allocation in hot loops (pooling)
nodes.rationale: Scratch vectors; pooled shells, particles, debris, lights and flashes; static obstacles merged into spatially chunked meshes to keep frustum culling; instanced shells; staggered AI decision updates.

nodes.label: 60 Hz fixed timestep with render interpolation
nodes.norm_label: 60 hz fixed timestep with render interpolation
nodes.rationale: Simulation steps deterministically at 60 Hz while rendering runs at display rate and interpolates tank and shell poses between ticks.

nodes.label: Simulation / presentation separation
nodes.rationale: Simulation is plain TypeScript (Three.js math classes only) and runs headless in tests; rendering, audio and HUD only read simulation state and consume the per-tick GameEvent list.

nodes.label: Local steering and unstick recovery
nodes.rationale: Enemies use local steering and avoidance instead of global path-finding; long walls can briefly trap them, after which an automatic unstick manoeuvre recovers. Coarse nav-grid path-finding is a listed future improvement.

nodes.label: One set of rules for everyone
nodes.norm_label: one set of rules for everyone
nodes.rationale: Player and enemies share the same Tank physics, weapons and collision code; enemies drive through the same throttle and turn controls.

nodes.label: Pointer Lock with graceful fallback
nodes.rationale: If the browser refuses Pointer Lock (some embedded browsers), mouse movement still aims and clicks still fire.

nodes.label: /graphify Trigger Command
nodes.rationale: Slash command that triggers the graphify skill; the skill instructions take priority over default behavior.

nodes.label: graphify Skill
nodes.rationale: Installed project skill at .claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md that turns any input into a knowledge graph; must be used before anything else when /graphify is invoked.

nodes.label: graphify explain
nodes.rationale: Used for focused explanations of a single concept.

nodes.label: graphify-out Knowledge Graph
nodes.rationale: Project knowledge graph stored in graphify-out/ capturing god nodes, community structure and cross-file relationships.

nodes.label: graphify path
nodes.rationale: Used for relationship questions between two concepts A and B.

nodes.label: graphify query
nodes.rationale: Returns a scoped subgraph answering a question, usually much smaller than the full report or grep output.

nodes.label: graphify update
nodes.rationale: Run after modifying code to keep the graph current; AST-only so it has no API cost.

nodes.label: GRAPH_REPORT.md
nodes.rationale: Read only for broad architecture review or when query/path/explain do not surface enough context, since it is larger than scoped subgraphs.

nodes.label: graphify-out/wiki/index.md
nodes.rationale: Preferred for broad navigation instead of raw source browsing when it exists.

nodes.label: Graph Rebuild Diff Policy
nodes.rationale: A committed graph.json is rewritten whole on every build, so large PR diffs are expected and must not be flagged as churn or used to justify skipping the rebuild or its hooks.

nodes.label: Graph-Query-First Rule
nodes.rationale: Run graphify query before the first grep/search/source read for codebase questions and propagate the rule into every code-exploring subagent prompt; raw files are read only for lines already located, because scoped subgraphs are much smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output.

nodes.label: Hidden-line removal (opaque solids + edge lines)
nodes.rationale: Every object has a near-black opaque solid that writes depth with polygon offset, plus crease edges (EdgesGeometry ~18 deg) and armour-panel outlines drawn as screen-space LineSegments2 with normal depth testing. Visible-face edges pass the depth test thanks to the offset; edges behind any solid fail it. Only structural edges are drawn, never triangle wireframe.

nodes.label: Fragment-shader terrain grid and contours
nodes.rationale: Grid and contour lines are computed in the terrain fragment shader so they are part of the surface: hidden-line correct by construction and immune to z-fighting.

nodes.label: favicon.svg (Vector Tank Icon)
nodes.description: 64x64 SVG browser-tab icon: a stroked, unfilled tank outline in cyan (#22e6ff) on a near-black (#02030a) square background.

nodes.label: Wireframe Tank Silhouette
nodes.description: Four line paths forming a side-view tank: tracked hull base (trapezoid), upper hull, turret, and a long gun barrel angled up and to the right.

nodes.label: Neon Cyan Vector Wireframe Style
nodes.rationale: Uses only unfilled strokes (fill none, stroke-width 3, round joins) in a single glowing cyan on a near-black background, matching the retro vector-display look implied by the game's VECTOR TANKS 3D branding so the tab icon reads as part of the same visual identity.

nodes.label: Seeded procedural battlefield
nodes.rationale: A ?seed= URL parameter replays a specific battlefield, and restart after game over reuses the same seed.

nodes.label: Quality presets with auto-reduce
nodes.rationale: Low/Medium/High trade resolution, MSAA, bloom and shadow-map size; auto-reduce steps quality down when FPS stays below 40.

nodes.label: Enemy perception (line of sight, hearing, reaction delay)
nodes.norm_label: enemy perception (line of sight, hearing, reaction delay)

nodes.label: Tactical map
nodes.rationale: Radar and tactical map deliberately show enemies hidden behind terrain because they are tactical UI; the 3D view never does (brackets only on enemies with clear line of sight). The map pauses the game by default.

nodes.label: Crosshair raycast with ballistic gun laying
nodes.norm_label: crosshair raycast with ballistic gun laying
nodes.rationale: A ray from the active camera finds the terrain, obstacle or tank under the crosshair, then the gun is laid with a ballistic solution from the real muzzle, compensating both camera-to-muzzle offset (important in chase view) and shell drop.

nodes.label: Enemy AI state machine
nodes.rationale: States Idle, Patrol, Investigate, Pursue, Attack, Flank, Evade, Retreat, Destroyed; kept as a pure, maintainable state machine so every transition is unit-testable and AI never touches rendering.

nodes.label: No-backend procedural static site
nodes.rationale: All geometry and sound are procedurally generated with no asset downloads, accounts or backend, so the production build is a static dist/ with relative asset paths that works from any host or subfolder.
